name: sub_second_burst
about: A burst-flood 300 ms long, placed inside one second and nowhere near its edges. Replayed twice from this one file: at the 100 ms cadence and at the 1 s cadence. The 1 s cadence spreads the same packets over 3.3 times the interval and reads 3.3 times less rate, which is the whole reason there are two cadences.
magnitudes: PARAMETERS. The burst is set at 1 200 000 over-budget packets per second for 300 ms, over a steady state of 6 000 per second, and the engine's burst threshold defaults to 500 000 per second. The arithmetic that matters is a ratio and not the absolute size: 300 ms of it averaged over 1 s is 360 000 per second, which is under the threshold, while any 100 ms of it is 1 200 000, which is over. Re-baselining the threshold against a real link moves both numbers together.

steps.note: steady state. Twelve periods, so the burst below starts inside the second period and ends inside it.
